_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2015: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2014 state of the verified 2014 register (China's ~3.5% objective of 5 Mar 2014; the RBI's CPI glide path of 28 Jan 2014, whose second objective, below 6 per cent by January of the following year, is the 2015 benchmark; the RBA's Statement of 24 Oct 2013, the FOMC's 2% goal, New Zealand's 2012 PTA, the BoJ's 2% target), plus the 2015 current-year targets set earlier (Türkiye 5%, CBRT policy document of 25 Dec 2012, para 19: 'as was the case for the 2013-2014 period, the inflation target for 2015 was set as 5 percent'; Brazil 4.5% ±2, CMN Res. 4,237 of 28 Jun 2013; Colombia 3% ±1, Board of 28 Nov 2014; Indonesia 4% ±1, PMK 66/PMK.011/2012 of 30 Apr 2012; Korea 2.5–3.5% for the three years from 2013, MPC of 11 Oct 2012), and the changes announced during 2015: Thailand's headline-inflation target of 2.5% ±1.5 (Cabinet, 6 Jan 2015, replacing the 0.5–3.0% core target), China's annual objective (5 Mar 2015: around 3%, from around 3.5%) and the Indian Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (recorded from the RBI Governor's statement of 4 Mar 2015, value unchanged at 6, because it replaces the row's wording). Value-unchanged reaffirmations (e.g. the FOMC's January statement of longer-run goals, the UK remit) and targets set during 2015 for later years are not recorded. Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: Two economies had no headline-CPI target at the start of the year: the Federal Reserve's statements refer to the PCE price index (see its row; the benchmark is applied to headline CPI), and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation until the Cabinet approved a headline target on 6 Jan 2015 (see its row). India's benchmark is the RBI's CPI glide-path objective. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, 25 Jan 2012: 'The Committee judges that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate.'
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy, 25 Jan 2012

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada, 8 Nov 2011: 'The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement was renewed for another five-year period.

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 8 Nov 2011

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 24 Oct 2013: 'both the Reserve Bank and the Government agree on the objective of keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 24 Oct 2013

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2007:3, October 2007
Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Policy Targets Agreement signed 20 Sep 2012: 'The agreement continues to require the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term. Within this target, the new agreement now requires the Bank to focus on keeping future average inflation near 2 per cent.'

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'New Policy Targets Agreement signed today', 20 Sep 2012 (Scoop)

CN.wording: Government Work Report delivered 5 Mar 2014: 'Consumer Price Index (CPI) increase will be kept around 3.5 percent' (the previous year's objective, which applies until the new annual objective is announced; a government objective, not a PBoC target).

urls.label: NPC (Xinhua), 'Highlights: Premier Li's government work report', 5 Mar 2014

IN.wording: RBI Third Quarter Review of Monetary Policy 2013–14, Governor's statement, 28 Jan 2014: the Dr. Urjit Patel Committee 'has indicated a “glide path” for disinflation that sets an objective of below 8 per cent CPI inflation by January' of this year 'and below 6 per cent CPI inflation by January' of the following year. The first objective's horizon is the current January, so the second (below 6 per cent, combined CPI) is the benchmark for the current year.

urls.label: RBI press release, Third Quarter Review of Monetary Policy 2013–14: Statement by Dr. Raghuram G. Rajan, Governor, 28 Jan 2014 (para 5)

BR.wording: CMN: 'É fixada, para o ano de 2015, a meta para a inflação de 4,5% (quatro inteiros e cinco décimos por cento), com intervalo de tolerância de menos dois pontos percentuais e de mais dois pontos percentuais'.

urls.label: CMN Resolution 4,237 of 28 Jun 2013 (2015 target)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: IMF Public Information Notice 07/140, Mexico Article IV, 13 Dec 2007
Banxico Inflation Report October–December 2007 and Monetary Program for 2008

ZA.wording: Budget Speech, 17 Feb 2010: 'I wish to confirm that the Reserve Bank will continue to pursue a target for CPI inflation of 3 to 6 per cent' (midpoint 4.5%).

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

TR.wording: End-2015 CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's policy document of 25 Dec 2012 (para 19): 'as was the case for the 2013-2014 period, the inflation target for 2015 was set as 5 percent as per the agreement reached with the government during the preparation of the Medium Term Program (MTP)'; uncertainty band ±2 percentage points.

urls.label: CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2013, 25 Dec 2012 (para 19)

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a symmetric ±1 percentage-point band, restated in the Monetary Policy Council's monetary policy guidelines (resolution of 30 Sep 2009, published 14 Oct 2009).

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007
MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

CZ.wording: 'The CNB announces the new inflation target as annual consumer price index growth of 2% (with a tolerance band of ± 1%), effective from January 2010'.

urls.label: CNB press release, 'The CNB's new inflation target and changes in monetary policy communication', 8 Mar 2007
CNB press release, 'The CNB issues Inflation Report I/2010', 12 Feb 2010 (the new inflation target of 2%)

ID.wording: Inflation target for 2015 of 4% with a deviation of 1%, fixed by Finance Minister Regulation 66/PMK.011/2012 of 30 Apr 2012 ('4% (empat persen) untuk tahun 2015, dengan deviasi sebesar 1% (satu persen)'; annual CPI inflation, year-on-year).

urls.label: Peraturan Menteri Keuangan 66/PMK.011/2012 on the CPI inflation targets, 30 Apr 2012

KR.wording: Inflation target set by the Monetary Policy Committee on 11 Oct 2012 for the three years from 2013: 'the range between 2.5 and 3.5 percent, in terms of the rate of change in the consumer price index' (midpoint 3.0%).

urls.label: Bank of Korea, 'Inflation Target for 2013 onwards', 11 Oct 2012

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

urls.label: Central Bank of Chile, Monetary Policy in an Inflation Targeting Framework, January 2007

CO.wording: Target for 2015 announced by the Board on 28 Nov 2014: it 'ratificó su compromiso con la estabilidad de precios al establecer la meta de inflación para 2015 en 3%, con un rango de ± 1 pp' … 'dicho valor debe ser usado para efectos legales'.

urls.label: Banco de la República, Board of Directors press release ('anuncia meta cuantitativa de inflación para 2015'), 28 Nov 2014

TH.wording: Core inflation target of 0.5–3.0% (quarterly average), in force since the Cabinet decision of 1 Sep 2009 (midpoint 1.75%).
TH.index: Core CPI; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Reuters interview with the BoT Deputy Governor, 3 Sep 2009: a new target of 0.5 to 3.0 percent agreed with the government
Thai Government, Cabinet meeting synopsis of 1 Sep 2009 (published 8 Sep 2009)
Kasikorn Research, 1 Feb 2010: 'within the BOT inflation targeting framework of 0.5-3.0 percent'
BoT Governor's speech of 24 Mar 2010 (posted 2 Apr 2010): 'our target range of 0.5-3.0 percent'

TH.wording: Headline-inflation target for 2015 approved by the Cabinet on 6 Jan 2015, as proposed by the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Thailand: 'an annual average of 2.5 percent, plus/minus 1.5 percent' (1–4%), replacing the core-inflation target of 0.5–3.0 percent.

urls.label: Kasikorn Research Center, 'New Inflation Target gives BOT Flexibility to Brace for Risks in 2015', 7 Jan 2015: 'On January 6, 2015, the Thai Cabinet approved a new inflation target'

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2015, main targets for this year: 'keep the increase in the CPI at around 3%' (a government objective, not a PBoC target; 2014's was around 3.5%).

urls.label: The State Council, Report on the Work of the Government, delivered 5 Mar 2015 (full text)

IN.wording: Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI: the Governor's statement of 4 Mar 2015 notes 'the release of the agreement on the monetary policy framework' and that the RBI will later seek 'the mid-point of the band of 4 +/- 2 per cent provided for in the agreement'; for the current year the glide-path objective of below 6 per cent CPI inflation by January of the following year (28 Jan 2014) remains the benchmark.

urls.label: RBI press release 2014–2015/1847, Statement by Dr. Raghuram G Rajan, Governor, on Monetary Policy, 4 Mar 2015
RBI press release, Third Quarter Review of Monetary Policy 2013–14: Statement by Dr. Raghuram G. Rajan, Governor, 28 Jan 2014 (para 5)
